title: Understanding Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a system by which individuals are categorized and ranked into hierarchical layers within society. These systems allocate unequal access to resources, power, and social opportunities across different groups.

The rigidity of these structures dictates life chances and the distribution of wealth, leading to inherent inequalities. Functionalist perspectives suggest that some levels of inequality are necessary to motivate talent and maintain societal efficiency, while conflict theories argue that stratification primarily serves to benefit ruling classes at the expense of marginalized populations.
